question.text: Look at the picture. Which solid is this?
question.explanation: Six equal square faces make a cube. A cuboid has rectangular faces that are not all the same.
question.alt: A line drawing of a solid with six equal square faces. Hidden edges are shown as dashed lines.

question.text: What is the name of the solid in the picture?
question.explanation: Six rectangular faces, with a length longer than the height, make a cuboid. A cube has six equal squares.
question.alt: A line drawing of a box-shaped solid with six rectangular faces, longer than it is tall. Hidden edges are dashed.

question.text: Look at the diagram. What do we call this 3D shape?
question.explanation: A perfectly round solid like a ball is a sphere. A circle is the flat 2D shape.
question.alt: A drawing of a perfectly round solid like a ball, with a dashed line around its middle.

question.text: Which word names the shape in the picture?
question.explanation: A dome with one flat circular face is half a sphere: a hemisphere.
question.alt: A drawing of a dome-shaped solid: a curved top resting on one flat circular face. The hidden back edge is dashed.

question.text: Look carefully at the faces. Which solid is shown?
question.explanation: One circular base and a curved side rising to a point make a cone.
question.alt: A drawing of a solid with a circular base and a curved side that rises to one point. The hidden back of the base is dashed.

question.text: Look at the picture. Which solid is this?
question.explanation: Two equal circular ends joined by a curved side make a cylinder.
question.alt: A drawing of a solid with two equal circular ends joined by a curved side. The hidden back of the bottom circle is dashed.

question.text: What is the name of the solid in the picture?
question.explanation: Two equal triangular ends joined by rectangles make a triangular prism. A pyramid ends in a point.
question.alt: A line drawing of a solid with two equal triangular ends joined by three rectangles. Hidden edges are dashed.

question.text: Look at the diagram. What do we call this 3D shape?
question.explanation: Two equal six-sided ends joined by rectangles make a hexagonal prism. A hexagon is only the flat end.
question.alt: A line drawing of a solid with two equal six-sided ends joined by six rectangles. Hidden edges are dashed.

question.text: Which word names the shape in the picture?
question.explanation: A square base with four triangles meeting at a point is a square-based pyramid.
question.alt: A line drawing of a solid with a square base and four triangular faces meeting at one point. Hidden edges are dashed.

question.text: Look carefully at the faces. Which solid is shown?
question.explanation: A triangular base with three triangles meeting at a point is a triangular pyramid.
question.alt: A line drawing of a solid with a triangular base and three triangular faces meeting at one point. Hidden edges are dashed.

question.text: Look at the four solids. What is the name of shape C?
question.explanation: Shape C is a cube. Six equal square faces make a cube. A cuboid has rectangular faces that are not all the same.
question.alt: Four solid shapes in a row labelled A, B, C and D: a can shape, a shape with a point, a box shape, a dome.

question.text: Look at the four solids. What is the name of shape B?
question.explanation: Shape B is a triangular prism. Two equal triangular ends joined by rectangles make a triangular prism. A pyramid ends in a point.
question.alt: Four solid shapes in a row labelled A, B, C and D: a pointed shape on a square, a tent shape, a ball shape, a long box.

question.text: Look at the four solids. What is the name of shape D?
question.explanation: Shape D is a cone. One circular base and a curved side rising to a point make a cone.
question.alt: Four solid shapes in a row labelled A, B, C and D: a pencil shape, a can shape, a pointed shape on a triangle, a shape with a point.

question.text: Look at the object in the picture. Which solid is it shaped like?
question.explanation: A camping tent: two triangular ends joined by rectangular sides.
question.alt: A drawing of a camping tent with a door, standing on the ground. It has two triangular ends and sloping rectangular sides.

question.text: Look at the object in the picture. Which solid is it shaped like?
question.explanation: A tin of food has two circular ends and a curved side: a cylinder.
question.alt: A drawing of a food tin with a coloured label band around its middle.

question.text: Look at the object in the picture. Which solid is it shaped like?
question.explanation: An ice cream cone narrows from a circle to a single point: a cone.
question.alt: A drawing of an ice cream: three scoops sitting on top of a crispy holder that narrows to a point at the bottom.

question.text: Look at the object in the picture. Which solid is it shaped like?
question.explanation: A dome-shaped building is half a sphere, with a flat circular floor: a hemisphere.
question.alt: A drawing of a round dome-shaped building with a small door, standing on flat ground.

question.text: Look at the cube. Which word names the part marked with the arrow?
question.explanation: A face is a flat surface of a solid. A cube has six faces.
question.alt: A cube drawing. One whole flat side of the cube is coloured amber and an arrow with a question mark points to it.

question.text: Look at the cube. Which word names the part marked with the arrow?
question.explanation: An edge is a line where two faces meet. A cube has twelve edges.
question.alt: A cube drawing. One straight line where two sides meet is thick and amber, and an arrow with a question mark points to it.

question.text: Look at the cube. Which word names the part marked with the arrow?
question.explanation: A vertex is a corner point where edges meet. A cube has eight vertices.
question.alt: A cube drawing. One corner point is marked with an amber dot and an arrow with a question mark points to it.

question.text: Look at the net. Which solid does it make when you fold it?
question.explanation: Six equal squares fold up into a cube.
question.alt: A flat net made of six equal squares joined edge to edge in a cross pattern.

question.text: Look at the net. Which solid does it make when you fold it?
question.explanation: One square with four triangles around it folds into a square-based pyramid.
question.alt: A flat net made of one square in the middle with a triangle attached to each of its four sides.

question.text: Look at the net. Which solid does it make when you fold it?
question.explanation: Three rectangles with a triangle at each end fold into a triangular prism.
question.alt: A flat net made of three rectangles in a row with one triangle attached at each end.

question.text: Look at the net. Which solid does it make when you fold it?
question.explanation: One rectangle with two equal circles folds into a cylinder: the rectangle rolls into the curved side.
question.alt: A flat net made of one rectangle with an equal circle touching its top edge and another touching its bottom edge.

question.text: Shape A is a circle. What is the name of solid shape B?
question.explanation: A circle is flat (2D). The solid, ball-shaped version is a sphere (3D).
question.alt: Two shapes labelled A and B. Shape A is a flat round shape. Shape B is a round solid like a ball.

question.text: Shape A is a hexagon. What is the name of solid shape B?
question.explanation: A hexagon is flat (2D). Two hexagons joined by rectangles make the solid hexagonal prism (3D).
question.alt: Two shapes labelled A and B. Shape A is a flat six-sided shape. Shape B is a solid with six-sided ends joined by rectangles.

question.text: Look at shapes A, B, C and D. Which one is a flat 2D shape?
question.explanation: Shape C is a triangle, which is flat (2D). A is a cone, B is a cube and D is a cylinder: all solid 3D shapes.
question.alt: Four shapes in a row labelled A to D. C is drawn flat with three straight sides. A, B and D are drawn as solids with depth and dashed hidden edges.
